## Proposal and provenance

Stable algorithm slug: `cross-channel-disagreement-salience`. Source: pm-4k6b note recorded 2026-07-30T09:24:36.574Z.

Catalog entry, by slug: cross-channel-disagreement-salience

Mechanism. The engine already scores candidates by metadata, graph position, history recency and usage affinity. This entry adds a signal that is not a property of any single item: the degree to which two independent recording channels that should agree about the same fact do not. Where they disagree, the disagreement itself is the highest-value context an agent can receive, because a divergence is exactly the place where the agent's model of the project is most likely to be wrong, and it is the one thing no single-channel read can reveal.

Channels the corpus already carries, all readable today. Item field versus history entry for the same field. Declared contract versus rendered help. Declared token budget versus measured payload. Item status versus the readiness the edge set implies. A relation written from one endpoint versus the same relation read from the other. Close metadata versus the release the changelog attributes. Each pair has a defined agreement predicate, so disagreement is computable rather than judged.

Scoring. For each candidate, compute a disagreement mass over the channel pairs that reference it: the count of violated agreement predicates weighted by how load-bearing each channel is for the current intent. Add that mass as an additive term to the existing relevance score, and attach the violated predicate to the candidate as its explanation, so a disagreement never enters the context window without saying what disagrees with what. Cap the term so a corpus full of legacy divergence cannot crowd out ordinary work - disagreement is a salience boost, never a sort key.

Required degeneracies, which are the acceptance conditions. On a corpus with one recording channel the term is identically zero and assembly is byte-identical to today. On a corpus where every predicate holds the term is identically zero. On a small workspace of a few items and a few minutes the term is zero because no divergence has had time to accrue, so the small end pays nothing for the machinery. Under a token budget the disagreement explanations degrade before the disagreements themselves, so the agent learns that something disagrees even when it cannot afford to learn what.

Why this belongs in the engine and not only in a gate. A gate can fail a build on divergence, but a gate runs on a schedule and reports to a human. An agent assembling context mid-task needs the divergence surfaced in the payload it is already paying for, ranked against the work it was going to do anyway. The whole method that produced this session's findings was manual cross-channel comparison; this entry is that method moved inside the assembler.

Interaction with existing entries. It composes with trust-weighted-context-assembly, which weights sources by reliability - here a channel that repeatedly loses a disagreement is exactly a channel whose trust weight should fall, so the two entries feed each other. It is distinct from refuted-and-abandoned-evidence-retrieval, which retrieves conclusions already rejected; a disagreement is unresolved, not refuted. It is distinct from recorded-order-arbitration, which decides which of two recorded orders to believe; this entry deliberately refuses to decide and reports the conflict.

## Delivery boundary

Evaluate this mechanism as a bounded public-SDK experiment before any production adoption. Use the existing scorer and packer contracts; no CLI-only behavior or new command noun. The historical catalog is design input, not evidence that this mechanism was implemented.

## Experiment protocol

Freeze a workspace/history revision and parameter manifest. Compare against the current deterministic SDK baseline using held-out judgments and negative controls. Report nDCG/action success, critical-evidence omission, latency p50/p95, peak memory, tokens per completed task, and rebuild cost separately. Include 3-item/minutes, real-shaped, 100k/1M-item, decades-long, and sparse/dense/imbalanced graph scenarios; smoke subsets may not claim scale acceptance. Bound candidate counts, graph expansions, elapsed time, and output size, with cancellation and completeness receipts. Record exact versus approximate behavior and approximation error; theoretical guarantees require their stated assumptions. Missing or untrusted evidence remains unknown, never inferred proof.

Promotion requires a reproducible quality improvement on the held-out target population, no regression of existing exact invariants or mandatory gates, and a declared compute/token cost justified by that improvement. Reject or defer with the same immutable evidence if those conditions fail. No production default, adaptive learning, or data export is authorized by this planning item.
